Class Section

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.Section
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public final class Section extends AbstractPanelElement
A collapsible section: a header row that opens and closes the elements under it. 
Section.builder(Component.literal("Shift-click"))
        .summary(() -> Component.literal(onCount() + " of 18 on"))
        .add(TextLabel.builder().text(Component.literal("Moves a stack to the other side.")).build())
        .add(checkboxes)
        .build();

Header

An arrow (▶ closed, ▼ open), an optional 8x8 colour swatch, the title, and a grey summary read every frame, cut with "..." when it runs out of room. A click anywhere on the header row toggles the section.

Content

Children are positioned from the top-left of the content area, which starts CONTENT_GAP below the header. They are laid out to the section's width the way a panel lays out its own elements (a label wraps, a Flow wraps, and growth pushes the children below down), and they receive input through ChildDispatch exactly as they would on the panel. A closed section's children are not drawn and take no clicks, wheel or keys; releases still reach them, so a drag begun before the section closed can finish.

Moving what is below it

Position the element after a section as if the section were closed. Open, the section reports its content as extraLayoutHeight(), so the panel's reflow pushes every later row down by exactly that much. Sections nest.

Open state: view state, or the consumer's

By default whether the section is open is its own view state, like a Tabs body's scroll: closed unless open(true), and kept for the life of the element (a tab's body is built once per menu, so switching tabs keeps it). state(get, set) hands it to the consumer instead: get is read every frame and a header click hands the new value to set.

Disabled look (§0066)

While disabled (its own disabledWhen, or its panel's or container's), the arrow, title and summary draw in the disabled grey, the header takes no clicks, and everything in the section is disabled too.

    • isInteractive

      public boolean isInteractive()
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Whether this element handles pointer input, so a point on it is a solid claim on a transparent panel. Controls return true; render-only decorations keep the false default, so they never eat a click they do nothing with.

    • render

      public void render(RenderContext ctx)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Renders this element at (ctx.originX() + getChildX(), ctx.originY() + getChildY()). When ctx.disabled() is true, an element draws its disabled look.

    • renderOverlay

      public void renderOverlay(RenderContext ctx)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Second-pass render for transient overlays that draw outside the element's layout bounds (a Dropdown's popover). Runs after every element's PanelElement.render(RenderContext), so an overlay is always on top regardless of declaration order. Pairs with PanelElement.getActiveOverlayBounds(InputContext), the input side. Default: no-op.

    • getActiveOverlayBounds

      public int @Nullable [] getActiveOverlayBounds(InputContext in)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      The screen-space bounds [x, y, width, height] of this element's active overlay (an open popover), or null when none is open. The dispatcher gives an element whose overlay contains the event exclusive ownership of that click or scroll, before any hit test, and the claim rule treats the overlay as claimed whatever the panel's opacity.
      Parameters:
      in - the element's input context (its origin, so it can place the overlay)

    • notifyClickOutsideOverlay

      public void notifyClickOutsideOverlay(InputContext in)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Tells an element with transient open state (a popover) that a click landed somewhere it did not claim, so it can close. The dispatchers call it on every shown element for every click, even one another element consumed; each element decides for itself whether the click was outside. Default: no-op.
